CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty swallowing

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Tyler is a 56-year-old male presenting with difficulty swallowing for 4-5 weeks. He reports sensation of something stuck in his throat that is occasionally painful. He notes difficulty with solid foods and has to wash them down occasionally with liquids, particularly foods like sandwiches. He denies complete choking but has worried about potential choking. Symptoms are primarily with solids; liquids are no problem. No temperature sensitivity noted. Denies hemoptysis, hematochezia, vomiting, weight loss, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies hemoptysis, hematochezia, vomiting, weight loss, chest pain, or shortness of breath. Denies coughing with swallowing. Denies nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea from metformin.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin 500 mg twice daily
Norvasc

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Neck: Normal, no swelling. Thyroid normal. No masses or lymph nodes. Throat: no masses, swelling, or redness. No carotid bruits. Lungs: clear. Heart: normal, no murmurs. Abdomen: epigastric tenderness, no masses or significant swelling. Back: normal. Extremities: normal. Neurological exam: normal.

RESULTS
Office blood pressure: 120/50. Previous hemoglobin a1c: 7.4. Patient reports home blood sugar readings within target range, checking approximately 80% of the time.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Dysphagia: Concerned for esophageal narrowing/stricture. Referral to gastroenterology for upper endoscopy. Start Prilosec 20 mg once daily. Recommend frequent chewing of foods, especially hard foods. Advise to seek emergency care if food becomes completely stuck.

Diabetes mellitus: Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily. Repeat hemoglobin a1c. Order blood work to check kidney function. Referral to ophthalmology for diabetic retinopathy screening. Follow-up in 1 month for lab results and possible medication adjustments.

Hypertension: Continue Norvasc. Patient doing well. Refill prescription to pharmacy.
